thread:
jamie-infra: seeing a spike of 502/504s from ap-southeast-1 since 03:12 UTC, p50 latency up 3x. metrics: https://grafana.redwood/2Wkpq -> gpu-pool-apse1 shows GPU mem pressure and lots of stalled requests

sasha-sre: yep alerts just fired. looks like BGP flap in carrier A affecting a subset of edge POPs, TCP handshakes timing out then retrying to same region. client rtt high + GSLB still favoring ap-southeast for some prefixes.

matt-runtime: can we temporarily change GSLB weights and lower TTL? prefer a soft shift to na-east with 80/20 split and ttl=20s to converge fast. avoid full drain to preserve affinity for long-running sessions.

zuo-network: agree on soft shift. also recommend enabling conn-ttl-smoothing to avoid hammering na-east pools. carriers show intermittent blackhole on 203.0.113.0/24 so avoid full redirect.

jamie-infra: propose commands:
```
# soft shift to na-east, lower ttl
gslb update-pool --pool ap-southeast-1 --weight 20
gslb update-pool --pool na-east-1 --weight 80
gslb set-ttl 20
```
I can run if ops+network +1.

ara-ops: +1. run canary for 5m and monitor 5xx rate, p99, connection errors. keep an eye on egress cost for na-east, this will bump inter-region egress for some customers.

deploy-bot: gslb change queued by jamie-infra. runbook ID: RB-APSE-BGP-2026. Will execute after 60s unless canceled.

jamie-infra: executing now.

deploy-bot: gslb changes applied: ap-southeast-1 weight=20, na-east-1 weight=80, ttl=20. timestamp=2061234728.

sasha-sre: initial telemetry: 5xx down ~70% in 1m, p50 back to normal for most prefixes. connection resets decreased. some long-lived sessions still to ap-southeast due to client caches.

matt-runtime: to reduce GPU pressure, can we enable model-fallback policy for ap-southeast routed requests: route to smaller-quantized variant (redwood-small-q4) when capacity > 85% mem. config snippet:
```
route-policy ap-southeast-1 {
  when gpu_mem_util > 85% then model = redwood-small-q4
}
```
This limits degrade impact without full user-visible fallback.

zuo-network: deployed conn-ttl-smoothing and adjusted GSLB health probes to 6s interval for affected prefixes. should stabilize session churn.

ara-ops: cost note: na-east egress estimates +12% for next 2h if traffic stays. Finance FYI: @finance-team may get pinged. we'll revert once ap-southeast path heals or after 2h.

jamie-infra: rolling monitoring window 15m. if errors < 5% and GPU mem < 70% in ap-southeast we shift back gradually. leaving soft-evac policy so customers with affinity keep sessions.

sasha-sre: followup: carrier reports partial fix at 03:40 UTC, but still elevated packet loss ~0.5% on same prefixes. recommend keep ttl low for another 30m then start 10% incremental shift back every 5m.

matt-runtime: agreed. also scheduled a transient autoscale bump for ap-southeast GPU pool (spin up 2 x spare nodes) to help with backlog; they are spot-backed and will be released after 1h.

deploy-bot: autoscale action issued: add 2 nodes to gpu-pool-apse1 (spot) - request id ASG-206123-9.

ara-ops: tagging incident: infra-2061-gslb-apse-bgp, severity: medium. notes saved to incident channel.

jamie-infra: thanks everyone. continuing to watch, will post update when we start shifting traffic back. :thumbsup:
